newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures end week on strong note.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures end week on strong note.

text.p: German Bund futures recovered strongly from a two-day slide on Friday as speculation about lower interest rates turned 180 degrees toward hopes of a cut in interest rates.
Comments from a pair of Bundesbank officials, Otmar Issing and Ernst Welteke, suggested that the central bank may yet cut rates if conditions allow, softening a stance taken only last Wednesday.
The hopes for lower yields left the Bund future up 30 basis points late in the day at 99.48, a sharp reversal from early declines that saw the contract touch 99.01.
"A lot of shorts got trapped when those comments came and the market got a bounce," said Harry Thapar, credit market analyst at MCM YieldWatch.
Analysts said they still doubt that rates will be cut any time soon, but comments from Issing saying he could not forever rule out rate cuts gave the market reason for pause.
The revived rate cut speculation led to a steepening of the yield curve as three and five year maturities gained favour.
The major event next week will be U.S. non-farm payrolls next Friday.
After several U.S. economic indicators this afternoon, the spread between T-notes and Bunds was nearly unchanged at 67 basis points.

Germany's six leading economic institutes could also give Bunds a bounce when they release their autumn forecasts. Predictions of a strong recovery from recent economic weakness could again smash rate cut hopes and hurt bonds.

Traders said they expect Bunds to remain in ranges at least until the data, adding they were encouraged this morning that the contract was able to hold above the psychologically important 99.00 level.
